Pop Best Bets 
GENTLE EXPLOSION-Jeannie Brittan- 
Decca DL 75054 
Young songstress Jeannie Brittan (18) 
sings sweetly and solidly on a set of eleven 
pop ditties. A highlight of the album is the 
gentle "Is This Love." "If I Could Only See 
You Once Again," "Blow Away Dandelion," 
and the title tune are other standout tracks. 
The lark, with her clear, vibrant tone, is like- 
ly to achieve favorable response with this LP. 
THE TRANSFORMED MAN-William Shat- 
ner-Decca DL 75043 
William Shatner, who stars on TV as Cap- 
tain Kirk on "Star Trek," makes his album 
debut with a series of narrations with cho- 
rus and instrumental background. This is an 
interesting "concept" LP; there are two 
narrations in each selection (except for the. 
title track) which are used to give multiple 
views on the same subject. Hence, the dejec- 
tion of "Spleen" is contrasted with the ex- 
uberance of "Lucy In The Sky With Dia- 
monds." Shatner's narrations are presented 
with effective drama, and the set is likely 
to receive considerable attention. 
Christmas Picks 
THAT CHRISTMAS FEELING-Glen Camp- 
bell-Capitol ST 2978 
This is Glen Campbell's first Christmas 
album, and it should please a wide audience. 
The chanter lends his talents to a program 
that includes such standards as "Have Your- 
self A Merry Little Christmas" and "I'll Be 
Home For Christmas," two new Sammy Cahn - 
James Van Heusen songs, "Christmas Is For 
Children" and "It Must Be Getting Close To 
Christmas," and a host of other engaging 
tunes. Should move well.

of favorites, which include "The Little Drum- 
mer Boy," "O Holy Night," "Silver Bells," 
"Toyland," "Have Yourself A Merry Little 
Christmas" and a Carol Medley. Should be 
an established air favorite come the Yule 
season.

MERRY CHRISTMAS-Raymond Lefevre- 
4 Corners of the World FCS 4257 
This LP by Raymond Lefevre and His 
Orchestra should brighten the Christmas 
season. Rich, lyrical instrumentations per- 
meate such traditional Christmas tunes as

CHRISTMAS WITH MAHALIA-Mahalia 
Jackson-Columbia CS 9727 
This set of seasonal favorites by America's 
best known gospel singer, Mahalia Jackson, 
should help to brighten the Xmas sales pic- 
ture considerably. The emphasis is on hymns. 
but several standards, such as "Silver Bells" 
and "White Christmas" are also present. 
Miss Jackson's version of "Do You Hear 
What I Hear" should receive heavy airplay. 
NOEL-Lennon Sisters-Mercury SR 61180 
The pleasant harmonies of the Lennon 
Sisters fill this enjoyable set of Christmas 
songs. The twelve melodies include "Have 
Yourself A Merry Little Christmas," "Do 
You Hear What I Hear," "Home For The 
Holidays," and "The First Noel." Singing 
with softness and grace, the Lennon Sisters 
should bring Christmas cheer to many a 
listener. 
Jazz Picks 
MILT JACKSON AND THE HIP STRING 
QUARTET-Verve V6-8761 
Vibist Milt Jackson is spotlighted on an 
album of eight jazz sessions, and his lucid, 
bell -like tones interact with a swinging string 
section composed of violin, viola, and two 
cellos. Included on the set are "You Got To 
Pay When The Deal Goes Down," "For All 
We Know," "A Little Too Much" and "Bags 
And Strings." The artistry of the musicians 
and Tom McIntosh's inventive arrangements 
make this a disk which should enthrall jazz 
fanciers. 
THE IN BETWEEN-Booker Ervin-Blue 
Note BST 84283 
Tenor sexist Booker Ervin serves up a set 
of six self -penned jazz tunes. The title effort, 
and "The Muse" are given a hard -driving, 
brisk treatment, while "Largo" and "Tyra" 
receive a smooth, lyrical reading. Backing 
up Ervin in fine style are Richard Williams, 
trumpet; Bobby Few, Jr., piano; Cevera Jef- 
fries, Jr., bass; and Lenny McBrowne, drums. 
This album should be greeted with enthusi- 
asm in jazz circles.

album.

PHIA/DE NATURA SONORIS-Cracow

Three works by the contemporary Polish 
composer, Krzysztof Penderecki, are pre- 
sented on this album. The most important of 
these is Dies Irae," an oratorio which Pen- 
derecki wrote in 19§7 in memory of those 
murdered at Auschwitz. This chilling and 
powerful work holds the listener in rapt, if 
somewhat frightened, attention. "Polymor- 
phia" and "De Natura Sonoris," two short 
works, the former for 48 string instruments 
and the latter for orchestra, are also of great 
interest.

Jack Lee Joins UA 
As Prof. Manager 
NEW YORK-Veteran music man 
Jack Lee has joined the United Art- 
ists Music publishing group as na- 
tional professional manager, effective 
immediately. Murray Deutch, execu- 
tive vice president and general man- 
ager of the operation, said that Lee 
will supervise all professional work 
for the group, which now includes the 
Metric 
Music 
subsid 
of 
Liberty 
Records. 
Lee was associated for a number 
of years with E. H. Morris as pro- 
fessional manager, where he was di- 
rectly involved in acquiring the copy- 
right to Louis Armstrong's 
two - 
million selling hit, "Hello Dolly." 
Earlier, Lee was professional man- 
ager of Meridian Music, prior to the 
sale of that catalog by Morris to the 
Lawrence Welk publishing interests. 
During his tenure at Meridian, Lee was 
instrumental in acquiring for the firm 
such memorable hits as "Canadian 
Sunset," "Land Of Dreams," "Van- 
essa," 
"Baby, 
You 
Got 
What It 
Takes," "The Stroll" and "Don't Let 
The Stars Get In Your Eyes." 
Before entering the publishing busi- 
ness, Pittsburgh -born Lee was an 
agent with Associated Booking.

Debuts In New York

TV/film packaging, including film 
scores. 
As president of 
Complex Three 
Ltd., Paul Jonali will coordinate all 
of the firm's activities. The Connie 
DeNave publicity firm will handle 
public relations and promotional ac-

duction will be The Children Of God, 
who are recording for A&M Records 
and will be produced by Howard Rob-

bia Records. While at Columbia, Rob- 
erts was responsible for producing 
Barbra 
Streisand, 
Tony 
Bennett, 
Diahann Carroll, and Bobby Scott, 
among others. 
The firm's BMI publishing arm will 
be called Complex Three Music. Writ- 
ers currently under contract include: 
David Perrett, Tony Mason, Bob Ron- 
denelli, and Jill Gorham. 
Complex Three maintains an open- 
door policy for new writers and new 
musical acts, as well as motion pic- 
ture and television properties.

Hispavox Wins Final Raphael Decision 
LONDON-The 
Hispavox-Raphael 
battle is finally over with Hispavox 
emerging the winner. The Spanish 
Supreme Court magistrate declared, 
"I must and do declare that the con- 
tract entered into by the parties on 
February 1st 1964 for exclusive re- 
cording of gramophone records is val- 
id and is in force and I must condemn 
and do condemn the defendant to re- 
frain from contracting the recording 
of gramophone records with any other 
company, national or alien, as far as 
said contract is not terminated, with- 
out prejudice of the use of the option 
right given to the claimant." 
Hispavox said that it was preparing 
to take the steps that the law allows 
concerning the nullity of the con- 
tracts signed by Raphael with other 
companies and also regarding the 
sales of records that said companies 
have been making. EMI has already 
withdrawn the "Ave Maria" single. 
Pye Records are licensees for the 
Spanish Hispavox label in the U.K.

A Golden Record is still news in

Heintje. The golden handshake was

Zeeland (insert). In Holland 12 -year - 
old Heintje still hasn't appeared on 
Dutch TV. In Germany, however, he 
will star in the Vico Torriani Show

strengthened greatly over the past 
year and a half. Sizing up this situa- 
tion is Lee Mendell, vp of Liberty, 
who just returned from a 3 -week tour 
of the label's licensees in Europe. 
Mendell's trip is a part of the in- 
ternational marketing concept at Lib- 
erty which calls for frequent high lev- 
el personal conferences with European 
offices. Mendell termed results "highly 
gratifying." 
"I was impressed," Mendell stated, 
"with the quality and calibre of licen- 
cee personnel. They possessed an 
awareness of the American music 
scene that many of us in the industry 
here might envy. Their knowledge 
of groups representing all companies 
and all labels was unbelievably exten- 
sive. They have fantastic knowledge 
of the whos, whats, wheres and whens 
of contemporary groups." 
Awareness of jazz trends is equally 
strong, Mendell says. "For this reason, 
the Liberty jazz labels-World Pacific, 
Blue Note and Solid State are getting 
outstanding action," he added. 
While Mendell was in Milan, the 
Solid State label was introduced into 
Italy by Tony Cassetta of Belldisc 
Italiana with ten releases. Reception, 
Mendell reports, has been excellent. 
The European jazz fancier's knowl- 
edge of jazz from old time to current 
is impressive, and the loyalty to art- 
ists is exceptional, Mendell said. "The 
jazz fan is more dedicated, more 
knowledgeable, and exhibits greater 
fidelity to artists than his American 
counterpart," he states. "Once they 
have taken an artist into their hearts, 
they keep him there." 
Mendell also reported that label 
key artists are exceptionally well 
known in all parts of Europe. The 
Canned Heat are currently on the 
charts in Norway, Germany, Holland, 
France, England and Denmark. Vikki 
Carr, Johnny Rivers, The 5th Dimen- 
sion, Classics IV, Bobby Goldsboro 
and Shirley Bassey also have excep- 
tionally large followings, he reported. 
Mendell participated in several dis- 
cussions regarding MIDEM. He states 
that Liberty will definitely partici- 
pate in the January 18-24 sessions of 
the organization. He terms this par- 
ticipation as of great importance. 
Mendell also indicated that he is 
even more convinced than ever that 
music is an international language. 
"Contemporary music," he says, "is an 
international happening, but the na- 
tionality of the group is not a factor 
in domestic release of the product." 
Releases of many of our European 
artists will continue to be domestic. 
Only ethnic music will be released 
through the U.A. International label. 
This is in keeping with Liberty's con- 
cept of World Wide marketing. He 
cited domestic release of German 
artist Suzanne Doucet who speaks- 
and sings-in fluent English as illus- 
trative of this concept. 
Mendell also reported that the Sun- 
set label is currently experiencing 
"tremendous" action in England.

CashBox Holland 
Two American singles on Bovema labels are doing very well in the Dutch 
charts: "On The Road Again" from Canned Heat on Liberty and "The Weight" 
from the Band on Capitol. This last single certainly will reach the top 10. Joe 
Cocker's "With A Little Help From My Friends" entered the top 10 after his 
strong TV promotion. The same can be said of the strong Hollies single "Listen 
To Me." As part of an European orientation from Liberty, V.P. Lee Mendell 
visited Bovema to talk about the Liberty sales and promotion. At the Amster- 
dam Hilton he gave the local press an insight in American record business. 
Bovema welcomed the American Folk Blues Festival 1968 in Amsterdam. Es- 
pecially the Blues -way artists T -Bone Walker, John Lee Hooker, Jimmy Reed 
and Otis Spann made a wonderful impression and did a nice deal in promoting 
this typical American repertoire in Holland. Good sales of these artists will 
certainly follow. 
The English group Simon Dupree & the Big Sound were in Holland for TV 
promotion of their smash release "Thinkin' About My Life." From Don Par- 
tridge Bovema rush -released his promising new single "Top Man." 
Label manager Theo Roos enthusiastically reports his new subscription action 
which consists of three boxes: "The Bach Concert For Harpsichord And 
Orchestra" played by Robert Veyron-Lacroix; "The Twelve Concertos Opus 
9 of Albinoni" with Pierre Pierlot and Jacques Chambon and the last a selection 
of piano works from the French school, "Florilège Du Piano" played by Jean 
Doyen. 
The publicity and advertising department of N.V. Phonogram set up a 
special promotion campaign for a new Decca single called "Now I Taste The 
Tears" by the Fearns Brass Foundry. With the help of every disc jockey in 
Holland, this amazing soul -ballad should be a smash. 
Holland is raving about the new single of the Equals. The group already 
had three big hits in Holland, but "Softly, Softly" will probably beat them all 
(President). 
On November 8th, N.V. Phonogram starts a huge promotion campaign for 
five albums of the Island label. New albums of Spooky Tooth, Traffic, Nirvana, 
Tramline and Jethro Tull will profit from special window streamers, folders, 
press kits, radio and TV approach, hand-outs, etc. Attention will also be 
given to new hit singles such as "A Song For Jeffrey" (Jethro Tull) and 
"Feeling Alright-" (Traffic). 
N. V. Phonogram released a beautiful four record set on Brunswick called 
"The Encyclopedia Of Jazz On Record." The four LP's include 48 tracks and a 
textbook with all info on the recordings. A rare item for the jazz fan. 
Blue Cheer's new album "Outsideinside" (Philips) was released just a few 
days before the group arrived in Holland to do four successful appearances. 
Dutch group Cuby & the Blizzards recorded a "live" LP during the Internation- 
al Pop & Jazz Festival in Düsseldorf (Germany). British blues expert Alemis 
Korner co -produced the record (Philips). 
The new Deram LP of the Moody Blues, "In Search Of The Lost Chord," 
is a bestseller in Holland. Fans are anxiously waiting for the single "Ride 
My Seesaw" which will be released by N.V. Phonogram in short time. 
Good news for Negram-Delta from the local productions department. The 
second LP by Christina Ciinne, singing songs of Greek composer Mikis 
Theodorakis, is obtaining high sales figures and has been received very well by 
local press and radio. A single by Tony Bass in the Dutch language, "Ik Ben 
Nog Niet Met Jou Getrouwd," has entered at No. 27 in the Dutch chart 
and is reported to take off in Belgium as well. Further the Neil Diamond 
composition "Red Red Wine," published by Shaltone and sung by Peter Tetteroo, 
is gaining tremendous airplay at both Radio Veronica and Radio Hilversum. 
The record is tipped for the top ten and was to be seen last week on NCRV-TV. 
Pye singer Long John Baldry visited Holland to appear in the AVRO-TV 
show "Doebidoe" to sing his potential top tenners "Mexico" and "When the Sun 
Comes Shining Thru." October 25 VARA -TV transmitted its "Puntje Puntje" 
show featuring Danish songstress Ann Tholsted doing "Master Jack" and Dutch 
Delta group Les Cruches playing their "Do You See The People." November 
1st NCRV-TV broadcasted the "Twien" show in which Peter Tetteroo sang his 
Red Red Wine" and Elektra artist David Ackles did his "Road To Cairo." 
New CBS additions to the single field include O. C. Smith's "Main Street 
Mission" as well as the original Russian version of "Those Were The Days" 
sung by the famous Russian singer Iwan Rebroff coupled with "Bessarabvanke." 
Most important LP release of this week is "Cheap Thrills" by the Big Brother 
& the Holding Company with vocals by Janis Joplin. Further issues in the 
popular LP field are Peaches & Herb's "Golden Duets," Ray Price's "Greatest 
Country Hits," Al Steward with "Bedsitting Images," the latest Miles Davis 
album entitled "Miles In The Sky." 
The Lowland Trio did it again. For the second time in two weeks the three 
boys of the CNR summer smasher "Ik Kan Geen Kikker Van De Kant Afdu- 
wen" appeared on television Saturday last. In "Pick Up" they introduced a 
sure top ten bomber: "Dikke Wand" (Thick Cheek). Irene Lardy, Dutch girl 
singer well known from a.o. Romeo & Julia, just returned home from the 
Austrian Song Festival in Innsbruck. Here she signed the contracts for 
several shows in Germany and Austria. CNR talent scouts discovered a new, 
tremendous good singer who will be a star in Holland soon: Marco Maas. This 
23 year old Rotterdam singer just finished his first recording: "Alles Wat Er 
Was" (All There Was). Gert Timmerman, six times gold and total sales over 
1,000,000 copies, recorded for the first time in his career songs for Xmas: 
twelve songs under the title "Christmas With Gert." 
The progressive firm of Dureco has as of November 1 two new record labels. 
Dureco got the whole Disc AZ repertoire for Holland with a.o. Michel Polnareff, 
Brigitte Bardot and Nicole Croisille. The new English label Morgan Records is 
represented in Holland by Dureco. This label has as famous English artists a.o. 
Chiitra Neogy, Voices In Latin, David H. Lee, Lenough Anderson, Jerry Allen, 
Harmonica Jewel Box, Ray Swinfield and Judd Proctor. Saturday October 26, 
Siw Malmkvist appeared in AVRO-color TV program "Lou Van Burg Show." 
In this program transmitted by Nederland II, Siw sang "Harlekin" and "Sady 
The Cleaning Lady." Dureco's producer Gert Timmerman has discovered an 
enormous talent, the 11 year old Wilma. She sings "Heintie Bau Ein Schloss 
Für Mich." This will be a 100.000 record. Dureco's Pink Elephant production 
"Ciao Baby," sung by Group Check, was last week to be seen in VARA's T.V. 
show "Puntje Puntje Puntje." Dutch pop singer Ben Cramer (Zai Zai Zai) 
was in Germany last week. In Hamburg his first record in German was re- 
corded and produced by the famous German producer Günther Henne. The 
A side was written by Marty Wilde, "In The Night." 
Former Polydor singer Pauline Kouwenhoven has set up her own publishing 
company in Holland called Intermusic. General Manager is Cees van Zitiveld 
who started his career as a D.J. for Radio Veronica and went into the pubbery 
with the houses of Altona and Belinda. The start of Intermusic was rather 
successful. They handle the publishing rights of Immediate Music Ltd. -London 
for Belgium and Holland, and negotiations with Monty Babson and Barry 
Morgan of Morgan Music Co. Ltd. -London went into the formation of Morgan 
Music Benelux. The offices of both companies are established at Herengracht 
4, Amsterdam, phone: 020-231390 
France 
Joseph Smith, General Manager for Warner Bros., came through Paris 
while touring Europe. Mr. Smith met with Leon Cabat, Vogue Records prexy, 
to strengthen the ties existing between the two companies. 
2 French artists were invited to the U.S. by Smith for cutting a record in 
the Warner Bros studios: Françoise Hardy and Antoine. 
Leo Missir, Riviera's Managing Director of Nicoletta, and Cyril Brilliant, 
Riviera's International Marketing Manager, went to London to set up with 
Philip Solomon's team the organization of Nicoletta's international promotion. 
They plan, after an impressive press promotion, the simultaneous release of 
Nicoletta's first single in English on the most important world markets, 
U.S.A., Canada, United Kingdom, EEC countries, Japan, Australia, South 
America and the Scandinavian countries. 
E. H. Morris publishing company communicates that Marie Laorêt register- 
ed a record ("Que calor la vida") a treatment of Frogat's song "Red Balloon" 
which is No. 5 in the British charts. Colette Deréal (Polydor) has cut a record 
of "Rowbutton Square" in French, "Quand la Fête est finie," lyrics, André 
Salvet. 
Jean Michel Riva, Frank Thomas and Jean Paul Orfino have just created 
a new production company Carabine distributed by Polydor. With the singer 
Jose Bartel (one of the voices of the film "Les Parapluies de Cherbourg") 
they favor the idea of the anonymous record. According to them, the song 
determines the sale of a record and not the singer. Their first 45 rpm is 
called "Fructidor" and this title applies to both the song and the group. The 
Carabine productions are promoting Jeanne Marie Sens as well. 
Liberty Records communicate that Ravi Shankhar is in Paris at the present 
time for his promotion. He will appear in the new French TV Variety Show 
"A l'Affiche du Monde." 
Claude Pascal, General Manager for NFC Music (his new publishing com- 
pany has his headquarters on the Champs Elysées no 34, Paris (8) telephone 
225 69 60. This address applies also to the Editions Essex and the Richmond 
Organization. Pascal is the manager in France of Enrico Macias who will 
leave soon for the States after having cut a record in Paris in Japanese. 
The Philips artists Les Freres Jacques have registered a live LP at the 
theatre Fontaine where they gave a new recital. 
The Equals stopped in Paris for the promotion of their new record "I Get 
So Excited." 
The music of the Paramount Film "Rosemary's Baby" by Normal Polanski 
is edited by the Editions Famous Chappell, and a record with the principal 
theme of the film by Hélene Montheral was released by Riviera. This song is 
titled "Tous les Trois Pres d'un Bercau"; lyrics by Michel Jourdan. 
The fifth Jazz Festival will be held in Paris from the 4th to the 8th of 
November. The most prominent artists are Horace Silver, Dizzie Gillepsie, 
Count Basie, Max Roach, Art Blacky's Jazz Messengers and Ravi Shankhar. 
Singer Dick Rivers has created his own record publishing company (D. R. 
Productions). Distribution will be divided among various firms. 
Henri Salvador, under his own label Rigolo, releases a new single of soft 
songs; main title "Copain Henri." 
Francis Blanche, the French comedian, has created his own publishing 
company, "Macheprot Records. Macheprot is the name he took when inventing 
his phone gags on the first French TV channel. This name has since become 
very famous. The first singer starring with Macheprot Records is Pierre 
Dudan who has just released a single and an album of very, very, sexy songs. 
Quickies: Jack Kerner, Polydor Prexy, lust gave a party for the release of 
Serge Reggiani's new record

RCA's president in Argentina, Robert Cook, reported to Cash Box that as of 
November 1 Adolfo Pino is the new General Manager of the Records area. 
Pino has been in charge of A&R and promotion. No A&R manager will be 
designated at this moment, according to the same report. RCA has its catalog 
divided into International, Folk & Tango, and Pop Music sections, with no 
changes in them. 
Juan Carlos Menna of EMI Suppliers reports that the first Apple single has 
immediately turned into a chart item. "Those Were The Days" by Mary Hop- 
kins is already appearing in the Top Twenty after strong initial orders. Now, 
Menna is expecting good results from the LP by John Rowles whose first 
single, "If I Only Had The Time," is still in the charts. According to extra - 
official reports (since this information is not made available to the press), this 
young company is currently in sixth place in the industry after only half a year 
in operation. 
Disc Jockey hosted a party to celebrate the tenth year in show biz of its top 
star, Rosamel Araya, at the plush Bamboche club. There was strong attendance 
from deejays, trade people and artists, and a musical show was also arranged 
for the audience. Disc Jockey's topper, Rodriguez Luque, reported that Araya 
will travel to Mexico soon to appear at the Song Festival planned in that 
country by Piero Bonino. 
Ricardo Davis, in charge of Promotion of new label Tolima, infos about the 
first releases under this label and the address of the offices: Tacuari 928, pisa 2, 
with Post Office Box 4270 at Correo Central for mail purposes. The manager 
of Tolima is "Toño" Muñoz Alvarez, and the first records are an album by 
Francis Morello, instrumental group, melodic chanter Lito Paye, and pop chant- 
er Amado Cortes. 
Beatriz Lupo from Relay Publishers infos that she will be present at the 
next Midem gathering in Cannes. The pubbery is working strongly on the 
promotion of local tunes, and several sub -publishing deals are being negotiated 
with countries like Germany, England, Japan and Italy featuring titles like 
"Tititando," "La Felicidad," and others. "La Felicidad" has already four record- 
ings in Italy, and others are expected in the rest of Europe. 
Manager Leonardo Schultz infos that British chanter Matt Monro will visit 
Argentina next month along with arranger Nelson Riddle. Monro has been en- 
joying success in the local charts via "The Music Played," sung in Spanish. 
and has several new songs ready for launching here. Another group represented 
by Schultz, the Tremeloes, are arriving in Buenos Aires in a few days, also 
singing in Spanish. 
The Press Dept. of CBS infos about the strong success of Leonardo Favio 
with his second single, selling about 110,000 singles in little more than four 
weeks. Favio recently made a promo trip to the province of Cordoba with good 
results and has finished his first LP. On the international side, the diskery 
is preparing the reception of Italian chantress Gigliola Cinquetti, who will 
spend about ten days in town appearing on TV. Alberto Caldeiro, head of the 
International A&R section of CBS, sends word about strong sales for the 
fourth LP cut by Brazilian group Lafayette with a selection of international 
current best-sellers. 
Mauricio Brenner of Fermata infos about the arrival of Brazilian topper 
Enrique Lebendiger who will arrive in town at any moment. Lebendiger will 
discuss several matters with Brenner, and mainly the expansion plans for the 
Record Division of the pubbery. Recent releases by Fermata include an album 
by Claudio Villa and singles by Sacha Distel, John Foster and others. 
Music Hall is releasing this week singles by US -group the Vogues, local folk 
chanter Rodolfo Zapata, melodic chanter from Ecuador Julio Jaramillo, and 
Venezuelan group Mario y Sus Diamantes. There is also a single cut by 
Johnny Albino, melodic chanter belonging for some time to the famed Panchos 
group. 
Hugo Persichini, manager of Phonogram, infos that the diskery will be mov- 
ing this week to new headquarters on Moreno 2038, the building formerly 
belonging to Korn Publishers and recently acquired by Philips. The diskery 
has also plans for new studios to be erected on top of the building and has 
ordered a video-tape outfit for promotional and artistic purposes. 
Hugo Guerrero Marthineitz is starting this week a series of shows at the 
Luna Park, the biggest indoor stadium in town, with a selection of top tango 
and folk artists. Among those taking part are Los Chal"haleros, the Cuarteto 
Vocal Zupay, Edmundo Rivero, Roberto Goyeneche and Horacio Salgan. Very 
low admission fees have been fixed for strong attendance. Guerrero is currently 
the most popular deejay in the country with five hours daily.

Dot Branches Expand Personnel Rosters 
LOS ANGELES - Dot Records has 
undergone extensive expansion at the 
distributor level. Numerous albums 
and a continuing program of contem- 
porary 
singles, including country - 
western, underground and teen -appeal 
productions, coupled with subsequent 
activity in the areas of sales and 
promotion, has prompted management 
to institute key personnel changes 
and additions throughout the United 
States. 
Ken Revercomb, Dot's director of 
sales and distribution, has disclosed 
these variations, which, in some in- 
stances were made from within the 
ranks. "A comprehensive study of our 
sales organization has been underway 
for some time now," said Revercomb. 
"It was based on a continuing flow 
of product, which we all know, rep- 
resents large investments of capital 
and creativity." He further said: "For 
these reasons, we must be certain 
that each release receives maximum 
concentration, and these changes are 
designed to assure just that."

years ago, honored Goddard Lieberson

recording Paul Robeson in "Ballau 
of 
Americans," Pete 
Seeger and 
"Songs from the Lincoln Brigade." tie

1y4ä.

in addition to his activities for the

STONEBLUES-Charles Musselwhite Blues 
Band-Vanguard VSD 792287 
Due to a resurgence of interest in white 
Blues, Charley Musselwhite's second album 
for Vanguard should stir up a considerably 
stronger initial sales reaction than his first 
effort. Musselwhite now maintains his own 
performing band, a definite plus, which has 
been attracting attention on the west coast. 
Another plus is the fine work of producer 
Barry Goldberg, himself a noted blues man. 
Tunes are mostly 
blues standards, but 
pianist/organist Clay Cotton contributes two 
strong new numbers. 
THIS WAY `IN'-Ronnie Aldrich/London 
Festival Orchestra-London Phase 4 SP 44116 
Ronnie Aldrich and his two pianos and the 
London Festival Orchestra have come up 
with another excellent album that should do 
well in middle-of-the-road circles. The full, 
rich sound of the artists, combined with the 
masterful Phase 4 recording technique, adds 
up to lots of good listening. Tracks include 
"This Guys In Love With You," "MacArthur 
Park," "By The Time I Get To Phoenix," 
and "Mrs. Robinson." 
THE SHENAI ARTISTRY OF BISMALL.
KHAN-Capitol ST 10513 
The shenai is an oboe -like Indian inst 
ment with seven open holes. On this albi 
Bismallah Khan plays the shenai with gr 
feeling and skill in three pieces, "Raga: 
hag," "Raga: Katavati" and "Dhun." M! 
albums of Indian music have been brou 
out in the U.S. during the past few yes 
this is one of the most interesting we 
heard. Try it. 
SANDY GURLEY-Tower ST 5135 
Sandy Gurley, displaying a bluesy, gu 
singing style, renders ten pop tunes. 
exception to artist's belting, brassy deliv 
is the lovely "Sometimes When I Get 
Thinkin'," which was written by Buffy 
Marie. "Handful," "If You Wanna Ride 
My Train," and "You Can Be Replaced" 
performed with power and zest. This 
could generate widespread interest in 
songstress.

THE CHRISTMAS WORLD OF SANDLER 
& YOUNG-Tony Sandler & Ralph Young- 
Capitol ST 2967 
Here is a most welcome album for the 
Yuletide season. Tony Sandler and Ralph 
Young bring their multi-lingual talents to 
three of the Christmas songs on the LP: 
"Susa-Ninna-Silent Night," a lovely tune 
in English with counter -lyric and melody 
sung in German; "White Christmas," sung 
entirely in Spanish; and "Jingle Bells," 
rendered in English and French. Filled with 
warmth and joy, this set makes a fine Christ- 
mas gift.

Classical Picks 
SWITCHED -ON BACH-Walter Carlos & 
Benjamin Folkman-Columbia MS 7194 
This highly significant album 
contains 
"electronic realizations and performances" 
of various Bach pieces on the Moog key- 
board synthesizer by Walter Carlos, with 
the assistance of Benjamin Folkman. Robert 
Moog, inventor of the Moog keyboard syn- 
thesizer, aptly sums up Carlos' achievement: 
"He has shown that the medium of electronic 
music is eminently suited to the realization 
of much traditional music, and in doing so 
has firmly brought the electronic medium 
into the historical mainstream of music." 
The set is part of Columbia's "Bach To 
Rock" classical promotion campaign.

Tower Names Sargent 
To Uptown Promo Slot 
IOLLYWOOD-Rich Sargent has joined 
Tower Records as promotion manager for 
the label's R&B subsid, Uptown. Sargent, 
whose previous experience includes a 
stint as promo manager for Action One - 
Stop in Buffalo and indie promo work in 
the same area, will be working in con- 
junction with Dave Fox, Tower's promo- 
tion director. He'll be headquartered in 
the label's Hollywood offices. 
In an additional move, Tower has 
named a new distributor for the Phoenix 
area, Endisco, who will handle all Tower, 
Sidewalk and Uptown product. Previous 
distrib was ARC.

Ochs Book Tops 8,000 
In Less Than A Month 
NEW YORK-Phil Ochs' new song book, 
"The War Is Over," which was pub- 
lished by Barricade Music a little more 
than three weeks ago, has already sold 
over 8,000 copies, a remarkable figure 
when compared with the sales of most 
song books. "The War Is Over" contains 
all the songs from Ochs' last three al- 
bums: "Phil Ochs In Concert," on Elek- 
tra, and "Pleasures Of The Harbor" and 
"Tape From California," both on his new 
label, A&M. 
"The War Is Over" was designed by 
Michael Ochs, Phil's brother and mana- 
ger. Michael used to work as a profes- 
sional photographer, and he has filled 
the book with striking pictures of Phil 
taken by himself and various other pho- 
tographers. "The War Is Over" also in- 
cludes drawings by the contemporary 
underground artist Ron Cobb and by 
Heinrich Kley, an article by Andy Wick- 
ham, four articles by Phil and a taped 
conversation made with him by Sis Cun- 
ningham and Gordon Fraser for Broad- 
side Magazine.

he record business. If ever there

Is that time is now. Too many

Sales Instead of Royalty Advances 
The formulation of new independent 
labels in jazz faces several obstacles, 
each of wnich could lie overcome with 
the understanding and co-operation of 
the jazz artist. Initially, it must be 
understood that the new label could 
not compete with the major when it 
comes to offering advances on royal- 
ties. It would be unrealistic to mini- 
mize the importance of money for the 
performer, but how he gets his money 
snould carry some weight, too. Is it 
better, from a career point of view, 
to receive a substantial advance and 
end up owing the label money because 
his albums didn't sell in sumcient 
numbers, or is it better to enter into 
an arrangement without an advance, 
knowing that the small company is 
going to extend every enort to make 
the album a success, botn nnanciafy 
and artistically? It boils down to tnis: 
is it better to be a big tish in a small 
pond, or a little fish in a big pond? 
Active Promotion from New Labels 
The principal difference between the 
small label and the large, from the 
player's point of view, should be how 
much time and energy will be spent 
promoting an album. I say album, be- 
cause jazz is essentially an album 
product. Rarely do we see a hit jazz 
single. When, as with a company 
which produces only jazz, an album 
is released it's safe to assume that 
every channel of exposure will be ex- 
hausted. It must, because that type of 
product is all they have to sell. How- 
ever, when a major label releases a 
jazz album, that release is usually 
concurrent with a large release that 
embraces many different types of 
music. Often the promotion man with 
the large company is expected to pro- 
mote his jazz release in concert with 
his regular product and, invariably, 
the jazz release suffers from a lack of 
effort. Think of the many excellent 
jazz albums that never get beyond the 
break-even point because of lack of 
promotion. Might we assume that if 
a smaller company had that album it 
would have enjoyed greater success? 
I firmly believe that if several en- 
terprising jazz producers would insti- 
tute some new jazz labels, and ap- 
proach things in the same manner as 
in the early Fifties, there would be a 
rebirth of interest in jazz recording. 
I 
also believe that the distribu- 
tors throughout the country would 
welcome these new labels, secure in 
the knowledge that they would receive 
every vital support from the label, 
something that they find very lacking 
at this particular time. Jazz is a 
special art and something that de- 
serves special treatment by people 
who not only have a particular devo- 
tion to the music but who will labor 
tirelessly to see that the fruits are 
enjoyed. If there are people out there 
who feel the urge and the need to in- 
fuse the jazz recording business with 
some "old" blood now's the time to do 
it!

DUKE ELLINGTON is presented the ASCAP Pied Piper Award for his 
"artistic achievements, for his personal qualities, for his loyalty and devotion 
to ASCAP" and for his musical talents. The inscribed trophy was presented 
by ASCAP president Stanley Adams last week at a dinner in Ellington's 
honor at the Hotel Americana in New York. He earlier was the recipient of 
this year's Ed Wynn Humanitarian Award on behalf of the American Parkin- 
son Disease Association. 
Publication Date 
Set For Books pan's 
'101 Masterpieces' 
NEW YORK-"101 Masterpieces Of 
Music And Their Composers," by 
Martin Bookspan, coordinator of sym- 
phonic and concert activities for the 
American Society Of Composers, Au- 
thors and Publishers (ASCAP), will 
be published by Doubleday on Decem- 
ber 6. The book, according to ASCAP, 
is "an in-depth treatment of the 
World's most popular concert works 
with emphasis 
on today's musical 
tastes." 
Bookspan has provided background 
notes on the creation of the 101 mas- 
terpieces, along with an interpreta- 
tion of their structure and meaning. 
There are also biographies of all the 
composers whose music is included 
in the volume. In addition, Bookspan 
describes the various recordings and 
tapes available and recommends for 
the reader the performance that he 
feels will afford the most meaningful 
musical and emotional experience. 
"101 Masterpieces" contains classi- 
cal works only and ranges from pre - 
Bach to the twentieth century. 
Bookspan includes a glossary of 
musical terms in his new book to- 
gether with a list of books for related 
reading and a check list of appropriate 
recordings. 
Bookspan is a noted radio and tele- 
vision music critic and commentator, 
a member of the music advisory panel 
of the U.S. Information Agency, a 
contributing editor of Stereo Review 
and a frequent contributor to other 
periodicals.

Record companies are becoming active in exploring the sales network of 
automobile industry. The music tape market, with 1 -track cartridge tapes 
its mainstream, has been showing a remarkable growth backed with 
increasing demand for car -stereo -tape players, and at present, 50% of the t, 
sales is brought through the distribution routes of automobile industry includ 
car dealers. Exclusive music tape makers, affiliated to the commercial broads:
ing corporations such as Nippon Hoso Service, Apollon Music and TBS Sery 
have been pushing into these routes since they started the business. If 
estimated that they share 80% of the music tape sales in this distribul
field, showing a rapid increase of monthly sales, although those record cl 
panies who have been mainly depending upon the existing record retail sys: 
are rising rather slowly. It is urgently required for record companies to enla 
the market by launching into the automobile sales networks.

Polydor Records made a considerable effort for the release and the promotion 
of Serge Reggiani's new album. This effort is explained by the fantastic 
success of his previous album which scored more than 250,000 records sold, 
which is an enormous figure for France. The new album includes songs by 
contemporaneous authors and one single with 2 poems by François Villon and 
Verlaine, the verses of which were set to music. Reggiani was just awarded 
in Brussels the Prize of the Music Critics' Association. 
Barclay Records, after CBSB, making a considerable effort for singles inter- 
preted by French artists. The single, which last year was adopted by all 
record companies for foreign records, has not up to now had great success 
with the French artists, apart from CBS. Barclay decided to follow the same 
policy as CBS and this week releases singles cut by Mireille Mathieu, Hugues 
Aufray, Alain Barriere, Henri Tachan. Mireille Mathieu, her new single, reg- 
istered in London 2 songs composed by Les Reed: "Ensemble," French lyrics 
by Bouquet, and "Les Bicyclettes de Belsize," French lyrics by Ithier. This 
record is produced by Les Reed. 
Philips publishes an album by the author -singer Serge Lama titled "D'aven- 
ture en Aventure." Lama, who was obliged to interrupt his career for two 
years after a very serious car crash, is the revelation of Bobino's new show. 
Claude François, under his own label Fleche Records, just cut a record of 
the French version of Ray Stevens' success "Mr. Businessman." 
Festival artist Gigliola Cinquetti releases in France "Quelli erano i giorni" 
which is the Italian treatment of "Those Were The Days." At the same time, 
CBS artist Ivan Rebroff has a good success with the Russian version of that 
song. Barclay Records doing strong promotion for the new Michel Dintrich 
record. Dintrich is presently the most popular artist (guitar) recording for 
the Barclay's Classic catalog.

Felix Lipesker of Korn Publishers infos Cash Box that this pubbery has 
acquired the rights to four publishing catalogs from the States: Borscht Music, 
Fling Music, Tridon Music and Kasket Music. The first three include not only 
Argentina but also rights to Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Peru, Paraguay and 
Uruguay, while the fourth doesn't cover Brasil. 
CBS has celebrated its Third Sales Convention with premiere of its Year End 
product which includes albums by top selling artists. Sandro will start shoot- 
ing a film soon, while Favio is planning a musical show and composing more 
music with Vico Berti, recently inked also by CBS. The diskery infos also 
that Brazililian chanter Roberto Carlos will visit Argentina next February 
to appear at the Carnival festivities and dance parties. 
Emi invited the press and deejays to night-club Goyo to be present at the 
performances of new melodic chanter Robertha, daughter of Peruvian chantress 
Fetiche. The diskery headed by Menna is releasing an album by the lark 
and has also launched the latest album by Johnny Rivers, "Realization," 
which is expected to sell strongly since Rivers' latest effort, "Live," is cur- 
rently in the charts. 
Odeon reports that it will be moving to new offices near tis factory in a 
few weeks and that new recording facilities will be made available soon at 
the same place. The diskery is now preparing the release of the recordings 
made through singles and an LP. On th International side, the effort goes 
on Franck Pourcel who recently visited Argentina and has had two singles 
recently marketed: "Those Were The Days" and "If I Only Had Time." 
Music Hall is working strong on the promo of Roulette artists Tommy James 
and the Shondells with a new single titled "Somebody Cares" and the featuring 
of them in an EP tagged "Greenwich Village" with the Loved Ones, the 
Fugitives, and the Choir. On the local side, the new recording by Rodolfo 
Zapata seems to have strong potential, as well as another LP by regional 
music artists Ambrosio Nicola. On the classical music field, the main feature 
this week is an LP by Henry Purcell, "Celestial Music." 
A whole carload of newies from Disc Jockey this week. Besides the already 
strong selling alubms by Rosamel Araya and Pepito Perez (and you can see 
Araya once more in the charts), there are singles by Elio Gandolfoi (cut by 
Carosello in Italy), the Geraldo Singers (produced by Major Minor), Odin's 
People (also coming from Maior Minor), Nicoletta (from the French Riviera 
catalog and Augusto Algueró (from Fonogram of Spain). The Rodriguez 
Luque label is currently willing to add more labels to its catalog, and negotia- 
tions are being held with diskeries from the States and Europe. 
RCA's Palito Ortega is currently shooting a film with Mexican chanter - 
composer Armando Manzanero, with lark Angelica Maria also having a part 
in it. The flick will have a double title: Corazon Contento" in Argentina, and 
"Somos Novios" in Mexico. Reason is that those were the biggest 1968 hits 
of Ortega in Argentina and Manzanero in Mexico. It is interesting to note 
that Palito is currently addig new artists to his record -production deal with 
RCA and is now producing the recordings by lark Violete Rivas, one of 
the three founders of the "New Wave" movement that in 1061 reshaped the 
whole local industry. Name of the record producing outfit is Producciones 
Chango, S.C.A., and it is located in the same place as Palito's pubbery, 
Clanort: Corrientes 824. 
Mauricio Brenner of Fermata is working hard on the promotion of the 
winner of the Rio de Janiero Son Festival, "Sabia." Spanish lyrics have been 
prepared and several local versions besides the original ones. On the record 
side, Fermata continues work on the recent John Foster single, and also 
on the PDU album cut by Mina, a big star in Argentina a few years ago 
when her "Studio Uno" RAI TV program was aired weekly here. 
Phonogram has released a good album by the Who under the Polvder logo 
as well as another single by the Bee Gees (I Got A Message For You) and 
a new one by Topo Gigio. It is worth mentioning that the Polydor logo has 
been gaining force in Argentina during the past moths through a string of 
best selling releases. A move stated by Hugo Persichini is that in the future 
kiddie music will be releasd almost xclusively on EP's, the format that 
seems to be the best one for this type of product. 
Recently launched label Doma infos about the release of new recordings 
by folk artist Juan de los Santos Amores, Juan Jose Herrera, Alberto Cuello 
and the trio Luz Y Sombra. Doma is currently devoted to local repertoire, 
but expansion into the International market is predicted for 1969. 
Mario Kaminsky of Microfon infos about a special products deal arranged 
with Aerolineas Argentinas, the state-owned air company, including a special 
record and a song performed by folk group Los Andariegos and devoted to 
the carrier. Microfon's Special Products Div. has been very active during 
these months, as well as the division of Microfon handling the Así budget - 
priced records, which have reportedly shown very good sales.

Sam (Musical Moments) Morrison 
would like the Federal Government to 
keep daylight saving time standard 
throughout the year. Sam says the 
early darkness these days can be 
dangerous to collectors who service 
machines 
located 
in 
"undesirable 
areas" of the city and recommends 
operators to schedule their stops there 
during the early part of the day. 
Sometimes there's nothing more at-

than a route truck parked in front 
of a bar, loaded with records, ciga- 
rettes and coins.

END OF AN ERA-Metro area 
operators will be saddened to learn 
of the death of veteran 10th Ave. one - 
stopper Eric Bernay last Sat. Nov. 
2nd. Eric, who was 62, suffered a heart 
attack the day before the annual vic- 
tory dinner of the UJA Music Divi- 
sion, the charity arm he organized 
three years ago. Eric has been identi- 
fied as the record man among the 
local trade who frequently visited his 
A-1 Record Sales outlet to buy their 
replacement records and to chat with 
the amiable Bernay whose "showbiz" 
talk always fascinated his friends and 
customers. He will be missed.

WB-7Sets ist Distrib Deal w/NewLabel 
NEW YORK-Warner Brothers -Seven 
Arts Records will soon begin to dis- 
tribute a label for the first time. The 
label is the newly formed Dove Rec- 
ords Company, a subsidiary of the 
diversified Hal Landers -Bobby Roberts 
film productions company. 
Announcement of this unique agree- 
ment-and arrangement-was made 
by Mo Ostin, company vice president 
as well as general manager of WB -7 
Arts' Reprise Records. 
Ostin additionally disclosed that the 
first release under the agreement 
would be a comedy LP recorded "live" 
by Richard Pryor. 
Pryor is the first artist put under 
contract by Dove. The Landers -Rob- 
erts unit plans to limit the number 
of recording artists it signs in order 
to maintain career direction for its 
artists in other media as well. 
Ostin emphasized that the W/7 
label entered into this association 
with Dove Records because of the 
structure of the Landers -Roberts or- 
ganization and the manner in which 
the two would function. He stressed 
that all record releases would main - 
Joe Rene Directs 
Purcell Publishing 
NEW YORK-Joe Rene has joined 
Gerard W. Purcell Associates, Ltd. in 
a major expansion move in publishing 
activities. Jerry Purcell, president, 
said Rene would serve in the newly 
created post of general professional 
manager to supervise all publishing 
activities of GWP Assoc., Ltd. Rene 
will work very colsely with young 
writers and maintain an open door 
policy to all newcomers, not only for 
GWP publishing companies, but for 
GWP clients Al Hirt, Eddy Arnold, 
Hugo Montenegro, Gale Garnett, The 
Hesitations, and many others. 
Rene will administer the following 
publishing companies: Hirt Music, 
Lupercalia 
Music 
Publishing 
Co., 
Rupel Music, all ASCAP firms, and 
Leprechaun Music, Five Sisters Music, 
Millbridge Music, Twin Forks, all 
BMI firms. 
Rene's talents as a producer, ar- 
ranger and conductor will also be 
utilized for GWP Productions, the in- 
dependent producing subsidiary of 
GWP Assoc., Ltd., which is headed 
by vice-president Paul Robinson. Rene 
has produced such artists as Peter 
Nero, Sy Zentner, Nina Simone, Paul 
Anka, Marilyn Maye, Joe Williams 
and was responsible for writing such 
hits as "Tossin' and Turnin" and 
"One Track Mind". He was most re- 
cently a pop A&R producer at RCA. 
SD Inks Dennison 
NEW YORK-Stereo Dimension Rec- 
ords, the new retail label of Longines, 
continues to build its artist roster 
with the signing of Homer Dennison, 
young 
(30) 
composer -orchestrator - 
musician. 
Bobby Byrne, A&R head of the 
company, said that Dennison was 
brought to the label's attention by 
Klaus Ogerman via an acetate of 
Dennison -produced 
sessions. 
Byrne 
found the sounds to be of "exciting 
commercial value." 
Dennison will be his LP debut on 
Stereo Dimension in Feb. It will be 
an album featuring a 40 -piece orches- 
tra in sessions utilizing 8 -track re- 
cording techniques. Most of the tunes 
will be originals by Dennison. Label 
is also planning on a possible singles 
release in Jan. 
tain a joint -label concept with each 
company's logo to appear. 
Dove Records plans to sign artists 
to the label who will encompass all 
styles on the contemporary music 
scene. 
Hal Landers and Bobby Roberts, 
who are extremely active in motion 
picture production have recently com- 
pleted their first feature at MGM, 
"The Gypsy Moths," starring Burt 
Lancaster. Their second film will be 
a Lee Marvin starrer, "The Die Hard," 
upon which work will be started in 
February at CBS Films. The company 
also has motion picture deals at Uni- 
versal, Columbia and MGM.

Thiele Organizes Flying 
NEW YORK-Bob Thiele has estab- 
lished Flying Dutchman Productions 
Ltd. Complex will encompass talent 
acquisition and record production plus 
such 
follow-through 
functions 
as 
promo, publicity, and merchandising 
as well. In addition, the new Thiele 
operation 
will 
incorporate 
both 
ASCAP- and BMI-affiliated publishing 
entities. 
Thiele said he will operate on the 
basis of a close and direct contact 
with the more youthful elements of 
the pop and jazz scene. This is where 
he feels the truly creative forces of 
today's music business are to be found. 
Initially, the new firm expects to 
complete contract arrangements with 
a number of key labels for the release 
of several new pop and jazz talents. 
According to Thiele, pacts with at 
least 10 leading companies are to be 
announced soon. Further negotiations 
are now underway for the organiza- 
tion of the firm's own label, to be 
operated on a joint ownership basis 
with a major company. 
It is envisioned that the Thiele or- 
ganization will undertake to produce 
artists already contracted to other 
labels. A brisk master acquisition pro- 
gram, under which masters will be as- 
signed to other labels for release, will 
Dutchman Productions 
also be a part of the operation. 
Yet another project involves the 
negotiation of a contract for release 
in the U.S. of Thiele's own New 
Happy Times Orchestra, previously 
issued here on the Impulse label. The 
Orchestra's original Impulse album 
will now be released in England by 
EMI, and Thiele plans to fly to London 
early in Jan. for a press reception 
given by EMI to launch the album. 
He will later fly to France to attend 
the MIDEM convention in Cannes. 
Prior to openings his new company, 
Thiele was associated for seven years 
with ABC Records as executive pro- 
ducer. He was also A&R chief for the 
ABC -affiliated Impulse jazz line, where 
he was responsible for highly sucess- 
ful outings by Albert Ayler, the late 
John Coltrane, and, more recently 
new West Coast guitar sensation Mel 
Brown. 
In straight pop, Thiele brought 
about a major comeback for Frankie 
Laine on ABC, starting with Laine's 
single of "I'll Take Care Of Your 
Cares." 
He 
was the producer of 
Louis Armstrong's most recent single 
hit, "What a Wonderful 
World," 
which became a number -one disk in 
England and an international million - 
seller. 
Decca's Current Vows High Voltage Future 
NEW YORK-Decca Records, taking 
its "New Directions-Tradition With 
A Future" theme to heart, heads into 
the last two months of 1968 with a 
strong collection of chart or chart - 
bound single and album product, and a 
strong November album release. 
On the pop singles scene, the firm 
is riding the charts with Leapy Lee's 
"Little Arrows," plus three decks on 
its Brunswick label, "From The Teach- 
er To The Preacher," Gene Chandler 
& Barbara Acklin; "For Once In My 
Life," Jackie Wilson; and "Just Ain't 
No Love," Barbara Acklin. Showing 
strong promise is "Soulful Strut," the 
Young -Holt Unlimited. 
On the country front, Decca is rid- 
ing with seven chart singles by Con- 
way Twitty, Bill Anderson, Leapy Lee, 
Loretta Lynn, Kitty Wells, Webb 
Pierce and Warner Mack. 
In the album division, the label is 
riding with "Magic Bus," the Who; 
and "All Hung Up," the Irish Rovers. 
In addition, Bill Gallagher, MCA vice 
president, Decca division, says that 
orders for the W.C. Fields album 
and the deluxe, two -record set of dia- 
logue and music of the original Lon- 
don cast of "Man Of La Mancha," are 
exceptionally heavy. Gallagher also 
noted that reaction to "The Light In 
The Wilderness," a two -record set 
featuring Dave Brubeck and the Cin- 
cinnati Symphony, indicates that the 
LP, released in September, is shaping 
into a strong sleeper. 
Three country albums currently 
moving up the charts are "Loretta 
Lynn's Greatest Hits"; 
"Next In 
Line," Conway Twitty; and "Happy 
State Of Mind" Bill Anderson. 
November Release 
For November, Decca is releasing 
11 new albums, including 5 country 
sets. The 5 pop sets are "Real," the 
Bag; "Fatha Blows Best," Earl Hines; 
a Broadway set from Carmen Caval- 
laro; "Easy Listenin'," featuring top 
Decca good music artists; and "Tran- 
sition," by Peter Duchin. 
The 
5 country sets are "Johnny 
Wright Sings Country Favorites"; 
"Love 
Take 
Care 
Of Me," Jack 
Greene; "Born To Be With You," 
Jimmy Newman: "Cream Of Country 
Hits," Kitty Wells; and "Country Hit 
Time," Ernest Tubb. 
Sole release on Brunswick is "The 
Gospel Soul Of Big Maybelle." 
Philips Releases Deluxe 
Double LP By 4 Seasons 
CHICAGO-Philips Records has re- 
leased a 2 -record set by the Four 
Seasons, 
entitled 
"Edizione D'Oro 
(Gold Edition)." The deluxe package 
includes 29 of the Seasons' chart sin- 
gles and contains a full color astrolog- 
ical poster. 
The actual LP cover done primarily 
in gold represents what is one of the 
most elaborate embossing jobs ever 
done on an album. Lou Simon, Philips 
product manager. said the label has 
formulated a major program on the 
promotion, advertising, publicity, and 
merchandising levels to insure success 
of the LP, which features all new 
remastering of the Season's hit rec- 
ords. 
A special merchandising display 
featuring the actual LP cover sup- 
ported by a "dual-purpose" card stat- 
ing "the deluxe gift album of the 
Seasons" is being serviced to retail 
outlets by Philips distributors. 
Blue Horizon Comes to US 
LONDON-Richard Vernon has ar- 
rived in New York to finalize details 
for the debut of the Blue Horizon label 
in America next Feb. He will also 
be setting up promotion campaigns 
to tie in with the visit of The Fleet- 
wood Mac in Dec. and January and 
The Chicken Shack next Jan. Vernon 
will be based in New York from Nov. 
8th to 21st and can be contacted at the 
newly set up Blue Horizon Inc. office 
at 146, West 54th Street. 
120,000,000 people. 
Ads 
Full -color roto spreads will appear 
in 31 key major -market newspapers 
and will feature the label's best-selling 
product, as well as new and standard 
Christmas 
LP's. 
Although 
these 
spreads will be the backbone of the 
campaign, they will be supplemented 
by ads in national trade and consumer 
magazines and coverage in under- 
ground publications. The Columbia 
series of ads will highlight product 
which will appeal to the audience of 
each of the various publications used. 
Ads being directed to reach followers 
of pop, contemporary, folk, country 
and jazz, as well as classical music. 
Columbia has also planned a nation- 
al spot radio schedule timed with an 
explosion of local dealer tie-in ads. 
Dealers and large department stores 
are receiving statement stuffers and 
over 5,000,000 full -color brochures 
will also be sent to them. Department 
and chain stores will feature lighted 
in-store Christmas displays. These 
units will include easels, streamers, 
mobiles, slicks ... the works.

Handleman's 5 Veeps 
DETROIT-Handleman Co., has ap- 
pointed of James Powers, Harold R. 
Scovill, 
Louis Kwiker, George H. 
Braun and Robert Cipriani as regional 
vice presidents. The five execs were 
all previously branch manager's for 
the 
company's 
record 
distribution 
centers in areas including Louisville, 
Ky., Pennsauken, N.J., Chicago, Ill., 
Dallas, Tex., and Toronto, Ontario, 
Canada. 
David Handleman, president, stated 
the new exec appointments reflect the 
company's program to continually 
"expand and broaden our regional 
distribution centers around the coun- 
try. 
Handleman Company is the largest 
independent wholesale merchandiser 
of records in North America. The 
company is also a wholesale merchan- 
diser of drugs, pharmaceutical, health 
and beauty aids and sundries, and 
operates a 17 -unit chain of discount 
retail outlets in Canada.

ASCAP's Billy Taylor To

NEW YORK-ASCAP has appointed 
Billy Taylor to the Society's Writers 
Advisory Committee, it has been an- 
nounced by Stanley Adams, ASCAP 
president. A pianist and recording 
artist, Taylor has been a writer -mem- 
ber of ASCAP since 1953. 
Born in Greenville, North Carolina, 
Taylor graduated from Virginia State 
College and has been a leading per- 
former in top clubs throughout the 
country. He has also had his own 
radio programs on WNEW and WLIB 
in New York, and is a member of the 
Advisory Board on Jazz for Lincoln 
Center. Taylor's songs include: "Mid-

I Knew".

Talent On Stage 
STEPPENWOLF 
BUDDY RICH BAND 
FILLMORE EAST, N.Y.-In the in- 
terim between Steppenwolf's first Fill- 
more appearance this past summer, 
and their second, last weekend (8,9), 
they rose from third act to headliners. 
They deserve top billing, and came 
over well, but for some reason, they 
didn't earn the nprmally super -en- 
thusiastic Fillmore audience response 
at the shows we caught. 
Perhaps one reason for the failure 
of a command encore was that the 
audience, waiting to hear "Born To Be 
Wild," didn't, and failed to realize that 
the show was over. To be precise, the 
group did get their share of applause 
after each number, said numbers in- 
cluding "Magic Carpet Ride" (their 
current Top 5er), "Sookie, Sookie" and 
"The Pusher," a tune off their first 
album that proved the most requested 
number of the night, in addition to 
several other blues standards and 
originals. 
There seemed to be a large number 
of Buddy Rich supporters in the rock 
house, and the vet jazz drummer was 
well received. Although his music is 
not in keeping with today's youth 
sound, his playing, and that of his 
band, is way- above par, and the Fill- 
more audience fully appreciated it. 
Tunes included "Mercy, Mercy," and 
an original, "Ruth." 
A&M's Children Of God were also 
on the bill, but the rain -slowed traffic 
caused us to miss them. 
VIKKI 
PERSIAN ROOM, NEW YORK-A 
year ago, Vikki Carr became a Persian 
Room performer on the considerable 
strength of the singles hit she and 
Liberty Records believed would some- 
day come her way. That song, "It 
Must Be Him," still serves her well 
today, yet, however, Vikki Carr de- 
serves to be a Persian Room act on 
the strength of Vikki Carr herself. 
This fact was very much in evidence 
at her opening there last Wed. (13). 
Sweet in looks and the things she has 
to say, the artist made it clear that 
impact can be generated without over 
doing it. Even the more dramatic num- 
bers, like her hit, "Yesterday I Heard 
the Rain," "Pen In Hand" and "Can't 
CARR 
Get My Eyes Off Of You" and "For 
Once in My Life," are recognized for 
their intrinsic worth and are not 
marred by, let us say, hand -wringing, 
acting-out gestures. Besides 
these 
contemporary items, there're also fine 
renditions of "More Than You Know," 
"Come Rain Or Come Shine" and "The 
Glory of Love." Also noteworthy is a 
fine ballad from "Dr. Dolittle" called 
"After Today." "Happy 
Together," 
the Turtles' smash, is effective as a 
jaunty vehicle for Miss Carr. After 
her third number, she said she would 
dispense with the normal routine of 
catching -one's -breath gab and sing 
instead. The audience was well re- 
warded with this display of confidence. 
DAVE VAN RONK 
TOWN HALL, N.Y.-Since splitting 
with his group, the Hudson Dusters, 
with whom he recorded an album on 
Verve -Forecast, Dave Van Ronk has 
returned 
to performing 
solo and 
worked up a repertoire that includes 
songs from a variety of sources, in- 
cluding his own head. Van Ronk has, 
against his will, been called a folk 
singer and a blues singer, but now no 
one could use either of those terms to 
describe him. Electrifying himself and 
working with the Hudson Dusters 
divorced him from his old ties, but in 
a way that didn't satisfy him. He de- 
cided to take up his acoustic guitar 
again and go it alone. 
By his own choice, his material, 
which includes songs by Jacques Brel, 
Brecht -Weill and Joni Mitchell, among 
others, has all but annihilated his 
image as a white urban blues singer. 
As he said genially to his Town Hall 
audience when some of its members 
requested his old numbers, "You're 
trying to destroy me. The man who 
did those songs was someone else." 
Van Ronk treats most of the songs 
he performs like miniature dramas 
and employs sudden volume changes, 
pauses and a variety of vocal and 
instrumental inflections to give his 
material dramatic impact. Sometimes 
his singing becomes talking or half - 
talking, and he may sacrifice the me- 
lody of a song to achieve the effect 
he wants. 
Among the songs he did at his 
November 8 Town Hall concert were 
"My Death," by Jacques Brel; "Moon 
Of Alabamy," by Brecht -Weill; "In 
Conditional Support Of Beauty," a 
brilliant composition of his own about 
the relationship between beauty and 
time and the dangers of trying to 
"abstract an object from a process"; 
Joni Mitchell's "Both Sides Now"; 
"Swinging On a Star"; and "Romping 
Through The Swamp"; Some of these 
songs are arrangements of numbers 
he did with the Hudson Dusters. 
For his encores, Van Ronk sang 
cappella two striking songs from a 
play he has just completed. The tunes 
are traditional Angio-Irish; the lyrics 
are Van Rock's own. The two songs 
are "The Last Call," a drinking song 
which he used as a farewell to the 
audience, and "Luang Prabang," an 
anti -war number. 
Dave Van Ronk has begun what is, 
in affect, a new career, and he has 
begun it on what seems to us to be 
very solid foundations. We wish him 
all success. 
JULIE LONDON 
EMPIRE ROOM, N.Y.-The plush 
Empire Room in the Waldorf Astoria 
Hotel provided the perfect setting for 
Julie London's opening 
on Friday 
night, November 
8. Miss London's 
sleek, 
sophisticated 
song 
styling 
DEE JAYS 
FROM THE PEN OF BOB GALLION 
"YOU REALLY KNOW 
HOW 
TO HURT A GIRL" 
& FROM THE PEN OF GERTRUDE COX 
"ONLY A STEP FROM HEART" 
by JOANN JOHNSON 
Trend 1044 
WORLD WIDE PROMOTION 
BILL MARTIN-Press Agent 
TREND RECORDS 
BOX 201 Smyrna, Ga. 
glistened luminously against the back- 
ground of the club's opulence. 
The Liberty recording artist opened 
with an up tempo rendition of "Hey, 
Good Lookin'," and then slowed the 
pace with "Makin' Whoopee." There 
is probably no one better qualified 
than Miss London to engage in the 
nuances of "Girl Talk," which was 
smoothly served up by the lark. She 
ixiformed the audience in a husky, 
sultry whisper that "Nice Girls Don't 
Stay For Breakfast," and later on 
rendered "Hello Dolly" in her own 
slow, sinuous version. 
Of course, the program would not 
have been complete without "Cry Me 
A River," the songstress' most famous 
song. After a segue into "The Man 
That Got Away," a highly inventive 
number closed the performance. Miss 
London sang the theme from the 
Mickey Mouse TV show in silkily, 
-sensuous tones, to the funky, soul 
accompaniment of her pianist.

NY Soul Showcase 
NEW YORK-A live talent showcase 
for soul acts, aimed at talent co- 
ordinators and producers in the TV 
media, has been set as a regular Mon- 
day night feature at the Village Gate. 
The showcase is being run by Jerry 
Purcell's Purcell 4 -Associates firm. 
Purcell stated that TV talent co- 
ordinators and producers had com- 
plained that they had been unable to 
see many soul acts perform in person, 
and even though many of them had 
outstanding recording successes, they 
were wary of booking them in a visual 
media. Purcell feels that this is a 
great boon to R&B artists, record 
companies and independent producers 
and all have indicated a desire to 
participate. 
Of equal importance to the record- 
ing artists is the fact that all disc

'Magnetic Film Recording' 
Touted As The Future's 
Process In The Present 
NEW YORK-A growing number of 
groups and performers have been 
making use of RKO Studios' facilities 
in New York, according to sound en- 
gineer Bill Blachley, because it is one 
of the very few which offers unlimited 
track possibilities as a major advan- 
tage. 
The key is in RKO's use of magnetic 
film as opposed to the more widely 
known magnetic tape. "Film," said 
Blachley, "is highly regarded because 
of its recording quality, but is even 
more important for its track and edit- 
ing features." These are less used be- 
cause of the initial expenses involved 
in establishing or converting the more 
conventional studios for film record- 
ing. "We worked with magnetic film 
because of our movie company affilia- 
tion originally, but with current de- 
velopments the technical aspect makes 
magnetic film studios especially im- 
portant." 
In a recent session the Serendipity 
Singers cut their "What Will We Do 
With The Child" on more than twenty 
different tracks. In regular tape stud- 
ios, this could only have been done by 
combining 
many 
of 
the separate 
tracks to free one of the pots for 
another take; but at RKO, the mag- 
netic film enabled each of the tracks 
to be kept intact. There is no 8 or 12 
track limit. Moreover, editing and 
splicing separate sections of the dif- 
ferent tracks into one another was 
made more exactly and with practic- 
ally no guesswork through the fea- 
tures of the film. 
"Had we used regular eight -track, 
or even twelve -track tape," noted Ser- 
endipity Mike Brovsky, "it would have 
been impossible to test and revise 
with all of the material from the tape. 
To use an extra track we would have 
had to combine or erase. Then, the 
originals would no longer be separ- 
able. At this studio, though, because 
of the film notations we could keep 
all we needed, slice sections and insert 
them from other tracks." The film is 
actually the same as 35mm camera 
film with its sprocket holes, and 
treated with a coating which enables 
it to be used for recording. Thus, the 
tracks can be zeroed in on for editing 
with no guesswork to an accuracy of 
a small fraction of an inch at first 
try. By noting if it is early or late 
between "frames," the exact point of 
slicing or transfer from one track to 
another for mastering can be located 
Bill Blachley at RKO 
more easily than with tape which must 
be done by ear and involves locating 
a switchover point or splicing point 
along the length of a foot indicated 
on the control indicator. 
"The way we work," Blachley com- 
mented, "editing is expanded from 
just combining entire tracks to editing 
in the moviemaker sense of clipping 
a frame and adding a section from 
another take, then possibly going back 
to the first, always maintaining the 
continuity." 
Unlimited Track Capability 
The unlimited track capability is 
made possible through the sprocket 
make-up of magnetic film. Not only is 
the surface larger (the entire film is 
used for recording, not just the movie 
sound track section), but because of 
the elimination of stretching and 
shrinkage, and the possibility of link- 
ing numberless film recordings to- 
gether accurately. 
Brovsky also pointed out that the 
recording quality of magnetic film is 
higher than that of tape. There is 
far less hiss and greater fidelity

Ed. B. Marks Acquires 
Rights to 2 Folk Masses 
NEW YORK-The publication rights 
for two folk masses, "The Daniel 
Jazz" and "Jonah -Man Jazz," have 
been acquired by Edward B. Marks 
Music Corp. from Novello and Co. of 
England. Marks Music has released 
both compositions for the U.S. and 
Canada. 
"The Daniel Jazz", based on the 
story of Daniel and his rescue from 
the growling lions and with words by 
the well-known American poet Vachel 
Lindsay, has a rollicking contempor- 
ary "pop" feeling in the music which 
is by Herbert Chappell. 
"Jonah -Man Jazz" provides a hu- 
morous narration of the story of 
Jonah and the Whale. Both its music 
and words are by Michael Hurd who 
originally wrote it for Bexley Erith 
Technical High School in England. 
Written in a free and easy style, 
both the compositions are intended 
as fun pieces for rompy singing by 
school or church groups. Guitar chords 
are provided and the piano score can 
easily be used for improvisation by 
some budding jazz instrumentalist.

recommendation of Jake Holmes." 
Holmes' latest Tower album, from 
which "Saturday Night" has been 
pulled for single release, was also re- 
corded at RKO. 
Although studies are constantly ex- 
panding to accommodate more -track 
equipment," Blachley commented, "the 
search and experimenting with new 
equipment is really unnecessary. Mag- 
netic film equipment is already here 
and able to out -track the others." 
"Many people reject film for tape 
simply because they are not used to 
the film idea. More rational opposition 
is based on the expense, which really 
prohibits the opening of a studio; but 
in a recording session the costs will 
ordinarily drop below those in taping, 
especially when it comes to a session 
with a lot of tracks.

Larry Yaskiel's Antenna promotion firm and Polydor joined hands for an 
important event last week. The start of the first tour of a German pop teeii 
artist and his one man show. The man was Roy Black who has sold millions 
of records here. The days of tours with a dozen or so pop singers is long gone. 
The halls are empty and the box office suffering from underexposure. Roy's 
tour of Germany was a sensational experience. The artist held down a 2 hour 
non-stop program with only the help of the Medium Terzett, a comedy -vocal 
trio who also record for Poiydor. A&R man Hans Bertram, who produces botn 
artists, put together a highly professional show and the halls were full. A 
great success tor Roy Black personally, and German pop music in general. 
Two very important events to promote pop music have taken place in 
Germany. r'irst, Deutsche Disc Jockey Organization boss Klaus Quirini has 
taken over as program director for "Radio North Sea," the new pirate station 
located off the coast of Germany. The station owned by Swiss business man 
Cesar Luethi and run by Norbert A. Gschwend will beam out pop programs 
from 5 A.M. until 1 A.M. with the strongest exposure due to fall on German 
language discs. The station should prove to be a powerful promotion tool for 
the record industry heer and a welcome supplement to Radio Luxemburg. o 
other D.J.'s have been hired to work on the station but the names are not 
known as of this writing. 
The second event is the publication of the bi -weekly pop newspaper "Sing - 
Sing." The paper has a strange ownership. 40 journalist joined to put up tue 
capital for the 4 color paper and hired top manager Stefan `on Baransky au,l 
former film journalist Erich Kocian to run the paper. The first issues are now 
on the stands and are selling very well. According to the management, it is 
thought to put out a weekly paper similar to the "Melody Maker," "Disc" and 
"New Musical Express" in England and to be the first and only pop paper 
directed to the fans. Germany has several trade papers but they are directed 
at the music shops and people in th trade. The "Sing Sing" sells for 50 pfennig 
(121/2¢), and the address for subscriptions and advertising is care of the editor 
Erich Kocian, 8 Muncih 83, Germany, Ulfilas Strasse 39. 
Teldec is going all out tor the new Hildegard Knef tour. The former movie 
star who made hundreds of Hollywood films is now a top chanson songstress 
here. The tour covering 38 concerts in as many days is heralded by a double 
LP with a special price tag of $7.25 (DM 29). On the 13 of November Miss 
Knef was awarded a golden record for sales exceeding a million records at a 
special midnight party after her concert. 
Ernie Bilkenrotn of Edition Marbot is doing the promotion thing for "No No 
No No No" from Scott McKenzie, "C'est Si Bon" from Louis Armstrong, 
"Inside My Love" from the Savages, French start David Christie with his nrs. 
German recording "Kleine Blaue Perlen" and "Dein Herz and Mein Herz" 
from Swedish songstress Britt Bergstroem. 
"Fiddler On The Roof" had its last Hamburg performance recently after a 
record breaking 26a snows. The musical is now playing Dusseldorf and will 
then go to Berlin on January 9th. 
One of Germany's top music journalists Dieter Broer will take over as head 
of the pop press department at Phonogram 'l'on as of January 1st. Hans - 
Henning Ganse is head of classical press and promotion for the firm. 
Publisher Peter Schaeffers called to say that Claus Ogerman was here a 
few days ago and took back a tremendous song called "Fuer mich soll's rote 
rosen regnen" or "Red Roses Will Rain For Me" written by Hans Hammer- 
schmid. Claus seems to think that the tun could be a smash in the states. 
Hildegard Knef sang it here and wrote the lyrics. 
Hans Gerig Music is all set for the new Carnival season which is now 
starting. The publishing house has new tunes to add to their fat catalog of 
carnival favorites and expects big business to result this year. 
Deutsche Grammophon has signed the Regensburger Domspatzen to an 
exclusive contract. Germany's most popular boy's choir are a very welcome 
addition to the D.G.G. team. 
Aberbach Music is going all out for "Midnight Confessions" from the Grass 
Roots. Other top push platters include "Quck Joey Small," "Keep On Loving 
Me Honey" from Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell, "Keep On" by Bruce 
Channel and "I'm In A Different World" from the Four Tops. 
Big record at present for both Liberty Records and Metric Music is "On The

AZ Records of France is making its debut in Japan under the exclusive 
repertoire contract with Nippon Columbia. The label features such French hit 
makers as Michel Polnareff, Christophe, Les Sunlights, Pierre Barouh and 
stars as Brigitte Bardot and Zizi Jeanmaire. The release is to be initiated 
with two singles, "Love Me Please Love Me" by Michel Polnareff and "Alou- 
ette" by Gilles Dreu and the albums of Bardot and Zizi Jeanmaire will shortly 
follow. 
The World Group Dept. of Victor has regained the exclusive distribution 
rights for the Vee Jay catalog which was released here by them until Septem- 
ber, '65, and then by Columbia until the bankruptcy of Vee Jay side. The 
contract this time is only restricted to the modern jazz best 15 items of the 
catalog, and the World Group Dept. is scheduled to release one album monthly 
starting with "Young Lions" by Lee Morgan Sextet. Victor -World Group 
has also signed an exclusive repertoire contract with Ranwood Records 
established by ex -president of Dot Records Randy Wood with such artists 
as Lawrence Welk Orchestra, Ray Anthony Orchestra and Damita Joe. The 
initial release of the label is Lawrence Welk's album entitled "Golden 
Lawrence Welk." 
Columbia is starting a monthly release of rhythm and blues material of the 
Buddah catalog with two singles: "Fool For You" by the Impressions, the 
group's first recording for Curtom, and "Don't Change Your Love" by the 
Five Stairsteps and Cubie. A new single on Buddah will soon be released, 
"Quick Joey Small (Run Joey Run) b/w Down in Tennessee" by Kasenetz-Kats 
Singing Orchestral Circus, the debut of the artist in our territory. Toshiba 
is rushing the release of "Those Were The Days" by Mary Hopkin. The 
Turtles' new single, after a long absence, "Elenore" has been just released by 
King. 
Grammophon is planning the Bee Gees' recent hits in a de -luxe album 
entitled "Idea/The Bee Gees" for a new -year release. The album includes "I've 
Gotta Get A Message To You," rising on the chart here right now, "Idea," 
"Kitty Can," "Jumbo," "Swan Lake," etc. On Verve, the double album of 
Astrud Gilberto will be out for release which will cover all her best hits such 
as "Girl From Ipanema," "Shadow Of Your Smile" and "Summer Samba." 
Apollon Music, an exclusive music tape maker, has announced the company's 
turnover for the half fiscal year between April and September, '68, to be 957.6 
million yen. The figure shows a 96% increase over that of the previous period. 
They are also satisfied with the result that 90% of the total sales has been 
attained by the Apollon's own products, while the other 10% is custom tape 
ordered by such companies as Fuji-tsu, Pioneer, Matsushita, Hitachi and King 
Records. In the previous period, the share of Apollon's own products and 
custom products was 65%-35%. This outstanding increase of the turnover is 
attributed to the success in the active promotion of the products under 
Apollon's own logo, of which 60% are the recordings of the artists belonging 
to Watanabe Production, as well as the recent rapid growth of the music 
tape market itself. Especially such local hit makers as Shinichi Mori and 
Yukari Itoh have contributed to the sales. The 8 -track cartridge tape has 
kept the leading position, sharing 90% of the turnover, while the rest is 
shared by music cassette. But next period they will take a more active steil 
into the music cassette market, aiming to make the share of 8 -track and 
cassette to be 70%-30% in future. 50% of the above turnover has been brought 
by the sales through the record retail system; 25% through automobile market 
including car dealers and 25% through filling stations and home electric 
appliance stores. Apollon has set the target for next six months (October. 
'68-March, '69) to be 1,200 million yen. They intend to attain the amoun' 
by developing the Apollon Shop system and other sales routes, on the 
distribution level, and on the production level, by launching new local artists 
and they are appropriating 40 million yen for investment in new recordine> 
facilities.
